posts.name: Jgraygaming2
posts.cooked:
In general, I prefer discussing strategy in chat rather than just clicking on a suggested card. I find "I can handle the environment because I have a grappling hook" to be better than just clicking on a card without saying anything. I'm especially not fond of people clicking on the card they think I should play every turn before I have even a moment to think about it. My thought? There's a single player mode if you want to control every aspect of the game.

That said, there are times when clicking on the suggestion works. For example, if Argent Adept is giving away a draw, card play, or power play, I'd say that's fair game to click on your name as short-hand for "I've got a really good play" but even then sometimes I'll follow up with "Got a grappling hook, team!"

posts.name: grysqrl
posts.cooked:
I'll second everything that Jgraygaming2 said. I try to use Suggest sparingly; I'd prefer to let people make their own decisions and use the chat to explain when I have a way to deal with a situation that they might not be aware of. I will occasionally use Suggest if I see an interesting combo, just to slow the other player down so I have a chance to explain in chat.

On the other side of things, when playing with a serial suggester, I usually make a game of trying to be effective while avoiding all of their suggestions. I find it incredibly annoying, especially if they don't bother to explain themselves.

posts.name: Bunston
posts.cooked:
Which is why I always play with the closed hands option! If you would like the input of the other players, than you can ask for it. Otherwise, it is much harder for an alpha gamer to take control of the situation if they can't see anybody's cards.

Just keep in mind that tablet users will probably be behind Steam users, so if somebody is taking a bit longer to make a decision, it could just be that they haven’t caught up yet, not because they don't know what to do.

posts.name: schadkehnfreude
posts.cooked:
In a vaccuum, it's always better to type thoughts in chat but as anyone with a slow iPad will tell you that isn't always... expeditious.  So in that context I'll sometimes chime in with suggestions in lieu of typing.  

If you click on the suggest button once in awhile, particularly for a tricky decision as to whether to skip a turn to off a particularly nasty environment, that's fine.

There was one time I told people beforehand it was my first time playing Chrono-Ranger so my two teammates suggested all the optimal plays since I'd never read his deck before.  That was fine and it was appreciated.

If I'm playing Legacy and you suggest without prompting each and every play I make, including whether or not to Galvanize when it's my only available power, then STFU I am completely disregarding anything you say from now until forever.

posts.name: riff.freelance
posts.cooked:
I, for one, like playing open hands to try and learn how other people play and make choices. There are some people that really feel like they are saying "hurry up and play" with their suggestions.  Chat would be really nice, but some people just don't explain ANYthing. 

For me as a general rule of thumb, I wait between 5-15 seconds before I start typing what I would do. Most of the time this gives people all the time they need. Also is how I would want to be treated. Sounds oddly religious, but I do default to the Golden Rule. I also find it helps to ask for advice in advance, usually during the environment and villian turns. 

For that matter talk more in general, you're playing a computerized version of a party game: act like you want to interact with people, or else play solo.

posts.name: Jgraygaming2
posts.cooked:
This got me thinking of the unspoken etiquette/rules of the game. Things like.

1. If there's a choice of who gets damaged, the person with damage reduction is the first target. Failing that, give it to the person with healing cards/powers. Exceptions can be made if said heroes are at extremely low HP.

2. When there's a choice to be voted on (to discard or destroy a card or to take damage, for example) and you aren't directly involved (none of your cards are options or your hero isn't in the mix) give the heroes who are involved a chance to decide before you vote. Its only fair to give one of them a chance to volunteer first.

3. If you have a way to get rid of a pesky card (environmental or ongoing, for example) say so in the chat as soon as possible. That way someone who goes before you doesn't waste a play, power, or entire turn to get rid of the card.

4. Order of effect matters. Don't just click on the 'choose for me' button without thinking it through. Sometimes you need to take out the card that's buffing other cards or that will damage you if other enemies are hit first.

5. Be patient. People are playing on different machines and on different platforms. Some people read at different speeds (and actually take the time to read the cards). Some people consider their moves before making them. Some people even like watching the game's animations as part of play. Respect each player's play speed.

6. Unless someone asks for it, suggesting every move for someone can be quite annoying. Especially when there's only one move available. Give people a chance to play their own character.
